title: Kernel + KV batching catchup (Jul 15–21, 2026)
content:
Quick summary: this doc collates the week's standups (Jul 15–21) for kernel work, KV cache experiments, and micro/continuous batching tweaks. Intent: sync cross-functional folks and record decisions + next actions.

Attendees (rotating): Priya, Marco, Leah, Omar, Jae, SRE on-call (Elena), product liaison (Sam).

What we observed this week:
- Micro-batching change (adaptive-window_v2) reduced tail latency for small chat workloads but regressed throughput for long-sequence cases. p50/p95 numbers: small-chat p50 38ms -> 30ms, p95 210ms -> 160ms; long-seq throughput -12% on the A100 pool (measured tokens/sec).
- KV prefill coalescing bug reappeared under bursty traffic from canary customers. Root cause likely race in the cache eviction callback when multiple kernels flush concurrently. Repro steps attached in linked jira (JIRA-RW-3124).
- Kernel patch (optimize-softmax-indexing) in PR 1987 improved single-request latency by ~6% on quantized models; no correctness issues found in smoke runs.
- Observability: trace correlator showed gaps where batching window was extended but no corresponding increase in requests — triggered by our heuristic probing logic. Means wasted wait time.

Decisions made:
- Roll forward adaptive-window_v2 only to dedicated staging fleets for 48h A/B test. Canary will be 10% of dedicated capacity. (Owner: Marco, due: 2026-07-23)
- Hotfix the KV cache eviction callback to serialize flushes per-shard instead of global lock to reduce tail latency and avoid long GC pauses. Implement as short-term fix; design a refined shard-coordinator in parallel. (Owner: Leah, PR target: 2026-07-22)
- Merge optimize-softmax-indexing into main for quantized path after one more regression run (Owner: Jae; regression window: 72h).

Open questions / items for design review:
- Should caching policy prefer prefix-key locality over LRU for chat sessions with streaming? Proposal: weighted LRU with session affinity; draft in confluence link. Feedback from SRE on memory impact requested.
- Backpressure interaction: when batching window increases to hit a throughput target, clients see higher latency spikes; need to quantify acceptable tradeoffs per SLO tier. Product asked for an automated policy mapping to customer tier. (Action: Priya to draft mapping by 2026-07-26)

Action items (concrete):
1) Leah: submit KV eviction callback hotfix PR and tag SRE for review (due 2026-07-22).
2) Marco: deploy adaptive-window_v2 to staging dedicated fleets and collect token-level cost and p95 latency for 48h (due 2026-07-23).
3) Jae: run full regression suite for quantized-optimize-softmax on all supported variants (bert-like, llama-2-70b) and report perf/correctness (due 2026-07-24).
4) Priya: draft SLO-tier to batching-policy mapping doc and circulate to product + SRE (due 2026-07-26).
5) Omar: add a short-term metric (wasted-wait-ms-per-request) to the console dashboard so we can quantify heuristic inefficiencies (dashboard ticket RW-DASH-57, due 2026-07-28).

Notes / quick wins observed:
- Turning off coalescing for requests with >2M token KV entries eliminated the rare 5–10s stalls in canary runs. We should add this as a temporary rule in runtime config.
- Kernel team found a low-friction optimization in the attention-kernel loop that reduces memory copies when KV cache is cold; small but cumulative improvement. Patch will be bench-marked next week.

Risks / mitigation:
- Deploying adaptive batching without proper canary could increase customer-visible p95. Mitigate via staged rollout + automated rollback at 10% p95 delta threshold.
- Hotfix could increase CPU usage per host; monitor host-level CPU and steal. SRE will set alert if 10-min CPU average increases >15%.

Misc notes / fragments (from meeting chat):
- "If we weight cache by session recency, we might starve multi-turn prompt reuse across clients" — flagged by Sam (product).
- "Add a synthetic ramp test that mimics bursty session joins + many small messages" — Elena (on-call).
- Link to benchmark artifact (temp upload): gs://redwood-bench/kernel-batch-jul21/summary.csv

Next sync: Wed Jul 28 09:30 PT. Separate design deep-dive for cache policy scheduled Tue Jul 27 11:00 PT.

Appendix (quick logs):
- Local repro steps for KV stall: run workload rw-kv-stall-sim with seed=83, set batch-size=8, prefill=true.
- Observed regression note: long-seq throughput regression tied to batch coalescing threshold=128; lowering to 64 restored throughput at cost of slightly higher p50.

End of catchup. If you want a shorter executive summary for product/legal, ping me and I'll strip the technical bits.
